images.note: Sequoyah, creator of the Cherokee syllabary (1821 beat). Primary: Henry Inman c.1830 copy after Charles Bird King (Sequoyah sat for King 1828; King original destroyed 1865), NPG, near-contemporary, CC0. Alt: later cabinet card of J.F. Standiford painting, 1850-1900, Gilcrease.
images.title: Sequoyah, creator of the Cherokee syllabary

images.note: Cherokee Phoenix front page, March 6, 1828 (1828 newspaper beat; shows Sequoyah's syllabary in print). Contemporary. LOC NDNP IIIF, 1324x2000. Alt: none qualifying at the bar (WCU holds the Feb 21, 1828 first issue but its viewer is JS-walled; Galileo/DLG 403). u4e7 uses the June 18, 1828 issue - different image, no collision.
images.title: Cherokee Phoenix front page, March 6, 1828

images.note: Principal Chief John Ross (1827 constitution / anti-removal leadership beat). Hand-colored McKenney-Hall lithograph ca.1843, SAAM, near-contemporary, Free to use. Alt: none qualifying (Denver Public Library holds a McKenney-Hall reproduction but its viewer is JS-walled; DAM copy has no image).
images.title: John Ross, Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation

images.note: Andrew Jackson (1830 Indian Removal Act beat). Thomas Sully 1845 oil, NGA, later depiction, 1678x2000. NGA promoted to primary because the NPG 1840 miniature collides with u4e3's Jackson entry (same image). Alt: none (NPG collides with u4e3).
images.title: Andrew Jackson, by Thomas Sully, 1845

images.note: Major Ridge, Treaty Party leader (1835 Treaty of New Echota beat). McKenney-Hall hand-colored lithograph ca.1838, SAAM, near-contemporary, Free to use. Alt: none qualifying at the bar.
images.title: Major Ridge, Cherokee leader

images.note: John Ridge, Treaty Party (Treaty of New Echota / 1839 killings beat). McKenney-Hall hand-colored lithograph ca.1838, SAAM, near-contemporary, Free to use. Alt: none qualifying at the bar.
images.title: John Ridge, Cherokee leader

images.note: Gen. Winfield Scott (May 1838 roundups beat). Robert Walter Weir portrait c.1855, NPG, later depiction. Alt: none qualifying (Hamilton College holds an 1846 Currier lithograph but eMuseum images are undersized; NPG c.1861 photo is same institution).
images.title: Winfield Scott

images.note: Martin Van Buren (1838 enforcement beat). Mathew Brady photograph 1855-58, Met, later photographic depiction, 3285x3993, public domain. Brady promoted to primary because the NPG Inman lithograph collides with u4e9's Van Buren entry (same image; u4e9 also uses the Met Inman oil as its alt). Alt: none.
images.title: Martin Van Buren, photograph by Mathew Brady, 1855-58

images.note: Osceola (Seminole War 1835-1842 beat). George Catlin, painted from life at Fort Moultrie, January 1838, SAAM, contemporary, Free to use. Alt: none qualifying (McKenney-Hall 'Asseola' exists in UC Libraries but their DRC viewer is JS-walled).
images.title: Osceola (Os-ce-o-la), Seminole leader, by George Catlin, 1838

images.note: Pushmataha (Choctaw removal 1830 beat). Charles Bird King, McKenney-Hall hand-colored lithograph ca.1837-44, SAAM, near-contemporary, Free to use. Alt: none qualifying (Delaware Art Museum c.1865 copy has only ~527px eMuseum images).
images.title: Pushmataha, Choctaw chief, by Charles Bird King

images.note: Mantle Rock, Kentucky - Trail of Tears National Historic Trail site where Cherokee detachments camped while waiting to cross the Ohio River (1838-39 removal beat). NPS photograph, 2304x3072, public domain. Alt: none (Cherokee Nation publishes route maps but only as PDFs, not images).
images.title: Mantle Rock, Trail of Tears National Historic Trail, Kentucky
